title: Optimize CPU-GPU handshake and threadpool to reduce host overhead during prefill/decode
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce host-side CPU overhead and wall-clock latency from prefill->decode pipeline by minimizing memory copies, lowering threadpool contention, and aligning kernel selection with real workload slices.

Background: Production traces show 20-30% of per-request latency at low-to-medium batch sizes is spent on host work: staging prefill buffers, scheduling kernels, cudaMemcpy roundtrips, and lock contention in the global threadpool. This is most visible for short sequences and multi-tenant shared GPU pools where we repeatedly submit small prefill chunks and immediately follow with decode kernels.

Scope: Changes target three areas: (1) CPU-GPU handshake (async submissions and fewer sync points), (2) memory-copy reduction (zero-copy / pinned buffers / reuse), and (3) threadpool behavior (per-device / affinity / lock-free queues). Work includes microbenchmarks, runtime changes, integration tests, and dashboarding.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Kernel submission batching: merge prefill chunk submissions where safe (same model config and device) to reduce kernel-launch overhead. Add a small adaptive coalescing window (configurable, default 1.5ms) to accumulate compatible submissions.
- Async path and fewer syncs: ensure prefill path uses cudaMemcpyAsync + cudaStreamSynchronize only when required. Convert blocking host waits to event-based callbacks so decode can be queued on the same GPU stream when data ready.
- Page-locked host buffers: switch ephemeral prefill buffers to pinned host memory (cudaHostAlloc) with a pooled allocator to avoid repeated allocations. Reuse buffers across requests to reduce allocation overhead and TLB churn.
- Zero-copy / GPU-resident KV caching: where model KV fits, prefer GPU-resident KV buffers and avoid round-trip copies for decode. Implement a fallback path that performs a single staged copy when memory pressure forces host staging.
- Threadpool redesign: introduce per-device io/submit threadpools to reduce cross-device locking. Move to a handoff queue (single-writer multi-reader) combined with a light-weight spin-once policy to reduce latency in hot paths.
- NUMA and affinity awareness: pin submitter threads to NUMA nodes closest to the GPU PCIe root complex to reduce cross-node memory latency on multi-socket hosts.
- Reduce syscall and metadata overhead: batch small memcpy calls into larger DMA-friendly chunks, minimize tracing calls on hot path, and provide a 'fast-path' compile-time flag to disable expensive profiling in perf-critical services.
- Kernel selection policy: add quick heuristics to pick fused attention kernels for short sequences and autoregressive decode kernels for long tail cases; expose an override map to pin kernel selection for experiments.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- End-to-end p50 latency for our 8k-context medium-batched benchmark reduced by at least 10% (measured on dedicated pool).
- Host CPU user-time per request reduced by >= 25% at steady-state.
- No regression in token-level throughput for large-batch workloads (+/-3%).
- No increase in GPU memory fragmentation or OOM incidents in weekly soak tests.
- New metrics emitted: host_submit_latency_ms, host_memcopy_bytes, threadpool_queue_depth, coalesce_window_us.

Tasks / Implementation plan:
1) Measurement: add microbench harness to simulate prefill->decode sequences with controllable chunk sizes and concurrency. Instrument existing pipeline to attribute CPU time by component.
2) Pinned buffer allocator: implement pooled cudaHostAlloc allocator with occupancy tracking and eviction. Add config flags to enable per-service.
3) Async submission refactor: refactor prefill codepath to use stream-based callbacks and remove implicit synchronizations.
4) Threadpool per-device prototype: implement per-GPU submit queues and handoff. Run perf tests to validate contention drop.
5) KV residency policy: add heuristics for keeping KV on GPU and single-copy fallback path.
6) Coalescing logic: implement adaptive coalescing window and safety checks (model mismatches, different key-shapes).
7) Integrations: add e2e tests, CI perf jobs, and Console dashboards for new metrics.
8) Rollout: gradual canary on dedicated pool -> dedicated large -> hosted small percentages.

Risks and mitigation:
- Increasing coalesce window may add tail latency if we wait too long; mitigate with adaptive window and per-customer SLO settings.
- Pinned memory can reduce host RAM available; allocator must enforce caps per-instance and monitor pressure.
- Per-device threadpools increase thread count; use lightweight fibers where possible and cap concurrency.

Notes: This ticket focuses on host-side overhead; model-level kernel code changes (e.g., attention kernel fusion internals) will be coordinated with the kernels team and split into follow-ups where necessary.
